_comment: Paste-ready node JSON for the n8n workflow `report_ingest` (id 3NRvDchKPT5RK4tn).
State as of 2026-09-09. Only the nodes on the ingestion path are here; the
error/alert branch and the sticky notes live in n8n.
THREE INVARIANTS, and every one of them was paid for with an outage:
1. ONE report email per execution (`Find Unprocessed Reports` is limit 1). Raising it
reintroduces the out-of-memory crash loop of 2026-09-08 - see AUDIT_PLAN.md A2.
2. The search is filtered to the REPORTING ALIASES, server-side at Gmail. A report a
person pulled by hand lands in their own mailbox, is not for the warehouse, and
3. Anything that still fails classification is ARCHIVED out of the inbox. Because the
sweep takes one newest-first email, an email that stays put blocks every older
report behind it - which is exactly what an all-jobs report addressed to
nicolas@ecomovers.com did on 2026-09-09, silently, until it was found by hand.
Plus: dbt rebuilds ONCE PER BURST. `Any Reports Left?` asks whether the inbox still
holds a report; if it does, this run skips the tail and the last run pays for it.
The tail is ordered drain-then-build on purpose: the resolved quotes must be in raw
BEFORE the build, or they wait for the next one.

nodes.name: Sweep every 2 min
nodes.notes: Every 2 minutes. A run that finds nothing costs ~0.7s and one that lands a report without rebuilding dbt costs ~15s, so frequency is cheap - it is the dbt rebuild that is expensive, and that now runs once per burst.

filters.q: from:no-reply@smartmoving.com subject:"Report is Ready" in:inbox newer_than:7d {to:reporting@ecomoversmoving.com to:ld.reporting@ecomoversmoving.com to:local.reporting@ecomoversmoving.com to:reporting@ecomovers.com to:ld.reporting@ecomovers.com to:local.reporting@ecomovers.com}

nodes.name: Find Unprocessed Reports
nodes.notes: Every report email still in the inbox AND addressed to a reporting alias. The alias filter runs server-side at Gmail, so a hand-pulled report sent to a person's own address never costs a download. Trashing on success is what makes the inbox the queue.

nodes.name: Shape Gmail Like IMAP
nodes.notes: Gmail's shape differs from IMAP's. One adapter here so Resolve Report Metadata stays untouched.

parameters.query:
-- One statement for the whole report. This used to be one INSERT per row, which
-- turned a 5,000-row report into 5,000 round trips - executions ran 20 to 30 minutes
-- and n8n held an item per row for the entire run. Set-based landing is the same
-- write with the same conflict semantics, in one call.
INSERT INTO raw_smartmoving.{{ $json.target_table }}
  (source_instance_id, entity_id, report_generated_at, row_key, row_data, _source_email)
SELECT r.source_instance_id,
       r.entity_id,
       r.report_generated_at::timestamptz,
       r.row_key,
       r.row_data,
       r._source_email
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS r(
  source_instance_id  text,
  entity_id           text,
  report_generated_at text,
  row_key             text,
  row_data            jsonb,
  _source_email       text)
ON CONFLICT (source_instance_id, report_generated_at, row_key) DO NOTHING;

nodes.name: Purge Legacy Row Keys

parameters.query:
-- TRANSITIONAL. Drops pre-2026-09-09 content-hash row keys once the same generation
-- exists under the deterministic position-only key. Never removes a generation's only
-- rows. Retire it when this returns 0:
--   SELECT count(*) FROM raw_smartmoving.report_payments WHERE row_key ~ '^__row[0-9]{6}__';
with dup_gens as (
  select source_instance_id si, report_generated_at g
  from raw_smartmoving.report_payments
  group by 1, 2
  having count(*) filter (where row_key ~ '^__row[0-9]{6}__') > 0
     and count(*) filter (where row_key ~ '^__row[0-9]{6}$')  > 0
)
delete from raw_smartmoving.report_payments p
using dup_gens b
where p.source_instance_id = b.si
  and p.report_generated_at = b.g
  and p.row_key ~ '^__row[0-9]{6}__';

nodes.notes: Transitional: drops legacy content-hash row keys once the position-keyed copy exists. No-op otherwise.

parameters.query:
SELECT
  $3::int AS expected_records,
  (SELECT count(*)
     FROM raw_smartmoving.{{ $json.target_table }}
    WHERE source_instance_id  = $1
      AND report_generated_at = $2::timestamptz) AS landed_records

nodes.name: Collect Emails To Clean
nodes.notes: One item per distinct message that landed successfully in this execution.

nodes.name: Find Email In Gmail
nodes.notes: Resolves the RFC822 Message-ID to a Gmail message id. IMAP gives us the header id; the Gmail API needs its own.

nodes.name: Move Email To Trash
nodes.notes: Adds the TRASH label to THIS message only. Never the thread - all reports share one.

nodes.name: Any Reports Left?

filters.q: from:no-reply@smartmoving.com subject:"Report is Ready" in:inbox newer_than:7d {to:reporting@ecomoversmoving.com to:ld.reporting@ecomoversmoving.com to:local.reporting@ecomoversmoving.com to:reporting@ecomovers.com to:ld.reporting@ecomovers.com to:local.reporting@ecomovers.com}

nodes.notes: Is another report still queued? The inbox IS the queue, so one hit means more work is pending and this run should not pay for a dbt rebuild.

nodes.name: Inbox Drained?
nodes.notes: TRUE = nothing left, so rebuild dbt now. FALSE = more reports queued, skip the rebuild and let the last run of the burst pay for it once.

nodes.name: Drain Quote Backlog

parameters.command: out=$(flock -E 99 -n /tmp/dw-quote-backfill.lock -c 'cd /home/datawarehouse_user/datawarehouse && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && ./venv/bin/python pipeline/run.py --job quote_backfill --dest postgres --budget 300 --pace 0.6' 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 99 ]; then echo 'quote_backfill: another drain is already in flight, skipped'; exit 0; fi; echo "$out" | grep -Ei 'unresolved quotes selected|load package|failed|Error|Traceback' | tail -20; exit $rc

nodes.notes: Resolves report Quote #s the API has never seen, newest first, 300 per instance. Runs BEFORE the dbt build so one build publishes the reports and the newly resolved quotes together.

parameters.command: out=$(flock -w 900 /tmp/dw-dbt.lock -c 'cd /home/datawarehouse_user/datawarehouse/dbt && set -a && . /home/datawarehouse_user/datawarehouse/.env && set +a && /home/datawarehouse_user/datawarehouse/venv/bin/dbt build --profiles-dir . --target dev --no-use-colors' 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$out" | tail -40; exit $rc

nodes.name: Find Unusable Email
nodes.notes: Resolves the RFC822 Message-ID to a Gmail message id so the next node can take it out of the inbox.

nodes.name: Archive Out Of Inbox
nodes.notes: Removes INBOX only - the message stays in All Mail, fully recoverable. NOT a delete. The inbox is the queue, so an email that cannot be ingested has to leave it or it blocks every older report behind it.
